name: The Covenant-Bound

identity.symbol: None known. Identified by fey bronze weapons and equipment distributed to humanoid proxies.
identity.public_perception: Not publicly known as a faction. The Bronze Host's escalation is visible; its Pact-Render backing is not. Most Tagmirans know orcs are pushing into the hunting grounds — they do not know why the orcs are suddenly equipped and coordinated.

goals.primary: Transform Airth into another Faery — using humanoids as tools to do the physical work of reshaping the world. They believe they can control the humanoids they arm. They cannot control men.
secondary: Exact revenge for crimes committed against fey by humans during The Deepening (years 100-150).
Ensure those crimes can never happen again — by making Airth inhospitable to the civilization that committed them.
Seize and hold the Bramblewood and surrounding territory as a fey-controlled perimeter.
goals.hidden_agenda: The Covenant-Bound believe they are using fire elemental power — specifically sun-metal — to their own ends. They are not. The fire elementals are using them. They do not know about the plan to ignite the moon.

philosophy.summary: Covenant-Bound elves have embraced their fey inheritance fully, severing themselves from mortal life to serve the Pact-Render. They are not the Gloaming Court — they are not ambivalent or desperate. They are committed. The Deepening was a real atrocity, and the world they want is one where it cannot happen again — even if that world has no room for the people who caused it.
methods: Command fey servants and lesser fey as a fighting force.
Fashion and distribute sun-metal weapons and equipment to humanoid proxies.
Arm and coordinate humanoid factions — Bronze Host orcs currently — as ground forces.
Glamour and manipulation of mortal actors who don't yet know they're being used.
limits: Will not work openly among mortals if it can be avoided — prefer proxy operations.
Will not break from fire elemental patronage, believing they are the ones in control of that relationship.

position.territory: Faery-adjacent locations, thinned-veil sites, and the territory they are actively seizing through humanoid proxies. The Bramblewood and surrounding hunting grounds northwest of Tagmira are a current operational zone.
position.active_since: Organized as a faction in response to The Deepening (years 100-150). Active in the current region for at least the past two months based on Bronze Host escalation.

alliances.nature: The Covenant-Bound believe they are drawing on fire elemental power for their own purposes. The fire elementals are using them. Neither side has disclosed the full picture to the other.

The Pact-Render supplies the Bronze Host orcs with bronze weapons and equipment via the Bronzeworking Triangle in exchange for territorial expansion. The orcs are the ground force; the Covenant-Bound provide the strategic coordination and materiel.

rivals.nature: Divine justice and fey transformation of Airth are fundamentally incompatible. Not yet in direct conflict but inevitable.
The Serdanos fear anyone anchoring Faery through belief or power — the Covenant-Bound's project is exactly that at scale.
Forsworn elves severed themselves from fey inheritance and oppose the Covenant-Bound's path. Active ideological enemies.

Both are fey factions but on opposite sides of the same politics. The Gloaming Court's goals and the Covenant-Bound's methods may be irreconcilable — undeveloped, but the Pact-Render and Aislith are likely not allies.

needs: Humanoid proxies willing to fight for territory in exchange for equipment and coordination.
Sun-metal supply from fire elemental sources.
Veil-thin locations to operate from and expand through.
provides: Bronze weapons and equipment — fey-forged, superior to standard humanoid gear.
Strategic coordination for otherwise disorganized humanoid warbands.
Fey powers and glamours in direct encounters.

pact-render.name: The Pact-Render
pact-render.role: Leader of the Covenant-Bound. A Covenant-Bound elf. The strategic mind behind the Bronze Host operation and the broader regional campaign. Identity and location undeveloped beyond the title.
pact-render.notes: Pact-Render shee have unknown fey powers. The Pact-Render's direct capabilities have not been established — develop before any encounter.

bronzeworking-triangle.name: The Bronzeworking Triangle
bronzeworking-triangle.role: The supply chain through which fey bronze weapons and equipment reach the Bronze Host. The mechanism — location, process, intermediaries — is undeveloped.
bronzeworking-triangle.notes: Why the Covenant-Bound can work sun-metal is an open question. The Bronzeworking Triangle is a potential adventure target — disrupt the supply and you degrade the Bronze Host's capability.

bronze-host-command.name: Bronze Host Command
bronze-host-command.role: The orc leadership of the Bronze Host — Brat-Kho, Mollgarn the Unfailing, and Ulzhar Bone-Tongue — coordinated by the Pact-Render. Currently pushing Tagmirans out of the northwest forest and making a play for the hunting grounds as the first step toward an assault on Tagmira.
bronze-host-command.location: Bronze Host tower, northwest of Tagmira
bronze-host-command.notes: All three named orc leaders survived the session 3 encounter. Equipment has since been upgraded via Pact-Render fey bronze. Each carries a magical item: Brat-Kho (obsidian glyph slab, booming voice), Mollgarn (spell-stealing plaque), Ulzhar (silver-wrapped fingerbone, command spell). Party departed the Bronze Host tower at start of session 26 — that arc concluded but the faction is still active.

bramblewood-perimeter.name: Bramblewood Perimeter
bramblewood-perimeter.role: The Bramblewood and surrounding hunting grounds northwest of Tagmira. The Covenant-Bound are seizing this territory through the Bronze Host. The Bramblewood itself was seeded by the old gods as a living perimeter — the Covenant-Bound's interest in it may go beyond the tactical.
bramblewood-perimeter.notes: The Bramblewood contains the Temple of the Old Gods. Its origin as an old-god perimeter is known to the Serdanos (Nabia held vigil here). Residual fey taint detectable only by a druid. The Covenant-Bound's control of this zone is the current early-game pressure point on Tagmira.

dm_notes: PRIMARY EARLY-MID ANTAGONISTS. The Bronze Host is the party's current visible enemy; the Pact-Render backing is the reveal that reframes what they've been fighting. The Covenant-Bound are being used by the fire elementals — this is a mid-game revelation and a potential lever: if the party can get the Covenant-Bound to understand they are tools, not masters, it creates a crack. The Gloaming Court and Covenant-Bound are on opposite sides of fey politics — Pima's Gloaming Court connection (mirror, Aislith) may be the party's window into this division. The Bronzeworking Triangle is a disruption target. Sun-metal properties need a decision before they become a significant plot element.
